p: an allusion from the Torah to visiting the ill?
“If these men die the common death of all men, … and … the visitation of all men, … From where … may … be inferred?

“If these men die the common death of all men, and be visited after the visitation of all men, then the Lord has not sent me” (Numbers 16:29). The Gemara asks: From where in this verse may visiting the ill be inferred?

p: Anyone who visits an ill person takes
let sixty … enter … and stand him up,
let sixty people enter to visit him, and stand him up,
like the tenths of the school of Rabbi … Furthermore, … one … same constellation

like the tenths of the school of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who said that each of one’s daughters inherits one-tenth of his possessions. His intent was that each daughter would receive one-tenth of the remainder after the previous daughter took her portion. Here too, each visitor takes from the ill person one-sixtieth of the suffering that remains, and consequently a degree of suffering will always remain with the ill person. Furthermore, visiting is effective in easing the suffering of the ill person only when the visitor is one born under the same constellation
